## Declaration

@property (nonatomic, copy, nullable) NSNumber * timedInvokeTimeoutMs;
```

<a id="discussion"></a>

## Discussion

If nil (the default value), a regular invoke is done for commands that do not require a timed invoke and a timed invoke with some default timed request timeout is done for commands that require a timed invoke.

If not nil, a timed invoke is done, with the provided value used as the timed request timeout.  The value should be chosen small enough to provide the desired security properties but large enough that it will allow a round-trip from the server to the client (for the status response and actual invoke request) within the timeout window.

Controls how much time, in seconds, we will allow for the server to process the command.

## Declaration

```swift
@NSCopying var serverSideProcessingTimeout: NSNumber? { get set }
```

<a id="discussion"></a>

## Discussion

The command will then time out if that much time, plus an allowance for retransmits due to network failures, passes.

If nil, the framework will try to select an appropriate timeout value itself.

# Document: timedInvokeTimeoutMs

Source path: documentation/matter/mtrmicrowaveovencontrolclustersetcookingparametersparams/timedinvoketimeoutms
Canonical source: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/matter/mtrmicrowaveovencontrolclustersetcookingparametersparams/timedinvoketimeoutms

# timedInvokeTimeoutMs (Swift)

**Framework:** Matter  
**Kind:** Instance Property  
**Availability:** iOS 18.4+ · iPadOS 18.4+ · Mac Catalyst 18.4+ · macOS 15.4+ · tvOS 18.4+ · visionOS 2.4+ · watchOS 11.4+

Controls whether the command is a timed command (using Timed Invoke).

## Declaration

```swift
@NSCopying var timedInvokeTimeoutMs: NSNumber? { get set }
```

<a id="discussion"></a>

## Discussion

If nil (the default value), a regular invoke is done for commands that do not require a timed invoke and a timed invoke with some default timed request timeout is done for commands that require a timed invoke.

If not nil, a timed invoke is done, with the provided value used as the timed request timeout.  The value should be chosen small enough to provide the desired security properties but large enough that it will allow a round-trip from the server to the client (for the status response and actual invoke request) within the timeout window.

# serverSideProcessingTimeout (Swift)

**Framework:** Matter  
**Kind:** Instance Property  
**Availability:** iOS 16.1+ (deprecated in 16.4) · iPadOS 16.1+ (deprecated in 16.4) · Mac Catalyst 16.1+ (deprecated in 16.4) · macOS 13.0+ (deprecated in 13.3) · tvOS 16.1+ (deprecated in 16.4) · visionOS 1.0+ (deprecated in 1.0) · watchOS 9.1+ (deprecated in 9.4)

Controls how much time, in seconds, we will allow for the server to process the command.

> Please use MTROTASoftwareUpdateProviderClusterNotifyUpdateAppliedParams

## Declaration

```swift
@NSCopying var serverSideProcessingTimeout: NSNumber? { get set }
```

<a id="discussion"></a>

## Discussion

The command will then time out if that much time, plus an allowance for retransmits due to network failures, passes.

If nil, the framework will try to select an appropriate timeout value itself.

# Document: timedInvokeTimeoutMs

Source path: documentation/matter/mtrotasoftwareupdateproviderclusternotifyupdateappliedparams-6s1jv/timedinvoketimeoutms
Canonical source: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/matter/mtrotasoftwareupdateproviderclusternotifyupdateappliedparams-6s1jv/timedinvoketimeoutms

# timedInvokeTimeoutMs (Swift)

**Framework:** Matter  
**Kind:** Instance Property  
**Availability:** iOS 16.1+ (deprecated in 16.4) · iPadOS 16.1+ (deprecated in 16.4) · Mac Catalyst 16.1+ (deprecated in 16.4) · macOS 13.0+ (deprecated in 13.3) · tvOS 16.1+ (deprecated in 16.4) · visionOS 1.0+ (deprecated in 1.0) · watchOS 9.1+ (deprecated in 9.4)

Controls whether the command is a timed command (using Timed Invoke).

> Please use MTROTASoftwareUpdateProviderClusterNotifyUpdateAppliedParams

## Declaration

```swift
@NSCopying var timedInvokeTimeoutMs: NSNumber? { get set }
```

<a id="discussion"></a>

## Discussion

If nil (the default value), a regular invoke is done for commands that do not require a timed invoke and a timed invoke with some default timed request timeout is done for commands that require a timed invoke.

If not nil, a timed invoke is done, with the provided value used as the timed request timeout.  The value should be chosen small enough to provide the desired security properties but large enough that it will allow a round-trip from the server to the client (for the status response and actual invoke request) within the timeout window.

## Discussion

# Document: timedInvokeTimeoutMs

Source path: documentation/matter/mtrotasoftwareupdateproviderclusterqueryimageparams-zidv/timedinvoketimeoutms
Canonical source: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/matter/mtrotasoftwareupdateproviderclusterqueryimageparams-zidv/timedinvoketimeoutms

# timedInvokeTimeoutMs (Swift)

**Framework:** Matter  
**Kind:** Instance Property  
**Availability:** iOS 16.1+ (deprecated in 16.4) · iPadOS 16.1+ (deprecated in 16.4) · Mac Catalyst 16.1+ (deprecated in 16.4) · macOS 13.0+ (deprecated in 13.3) · tvOS 16.1+ (deprecated in 16.4) · visionOS 1.0+ (deprecated in 1.0) · watchOS 9.1+ (deprecated in 9.4)

Controls whether the command is a timed command (using Timed Invoke).

> Please use MTROTASoftwareUpdateProviderClusterQueryImageParams

## Declaration

```swift
@NSCopying var timedInvokeTimeoutMs: NSNumber? { get set }
```

<a id="discussion"></a>

## Discussion

If nil (the default value), a regular invoke is done for commands that do not require a timed invoke and a timed invoke with some default timed request timeout is done for commands that require a timed invoke.

If not nil, a timed invoke is done, with the provided value used as the timed request timeout.  The value should be chosen small enough to provide the desired security properties but large enough that it will allow a round-trip from the server to the client (for the status response and actual invoke request) within the timeout window.

## Discussion

The value should be chosen small enough to provide the desired security properties but large enough that it will allow a round-trip from the server to the client (for the status response and actual invoke request) within the timeout window.

# serverSideProcessingTimeout (Swift)

**Framework:** Matter  
**Kind:** Instance Property  
**Availability:** iOS 16.1+ (deprecated in 16.4) · iPadOS 16.1+ (deprecated in 16.4) · Mac Catalyst 16.1+ (deprecated in 16.4) · macOS 13.0+ (deprecated in 13.3) · tvOS 16.1+ (deprecated in 16.4) · visionOS 1.0+ (deprecated in 1.0) · watchOS 9.1+ (deprecated in 9.4)

Controls how much time, in seconds, we will allow for the server to process the command.

> Please use MTROTASoftwareUpdateRequestorClusterAnnounceOTAProviderParams

## Declaration

```swift
@NSCopying var serverSideProcessingTimeout: NSNumber? { get set }
```

<a id="discussion"></a>

## Discussion

The command will then time out if that much time, plus an allowance for retransmits due to network failures, passes.

If nil, the framework will try to select an appropriate timeout value itself.

# Document: timedInvokeTimeoutMs

Source path: documentation/matter/mtrotasoftwareupdaterequestorclusterannounceotaproviderparams-8dobu/timedinvoketimeoutms
Canonical source: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/matter/mtrotasoftwareupdaterequestorclusterannounceotaproviderparams-8dobu/timedinvoketimeoutms

# timedInvokeTimeoutMs (Swift)

**Framework:** Matter  
**Kind:** Instance Property  
**Availability:** iOS 16.4+ · iPadOS 16.4+ · Mac Catalyst 16.4+ · macOS 13.3+ · tvOS 16.4+ · visionOS 1.0+ · watchOS 9.4+

Controls whether the command is a timed command (using Timed Invoke).

## Declaration

```swift
@NSCopying var timedInvokeTimeoutMs: NSNumber? { get set }
```

<a id="discussion"></a>

## Discussion

If nil (the default value), a regular invoke is done for commands that do not require a timed invoke and a timed invoke with some default timed request timeout is done for commands that require a timed invoke.

If not nil, a timed invoke is done, with the provided value used as the timed request timeout.  The value should be chosen small enough to provide the desired security properties but large enough that it will allow a round-trip from the server to the client (for the status response and actual invoke request) within the timeout window.

# timedInvokeTimeoutMs (Objective-C)

**Framework:** Matter  
**Kind:** Instance Property  
**Availability:** iOS 16.4+ · iPadOS 16.4+ · Mac Catalyst 16.4+ · macOS 13.3+ · tvOS 16.4+ · visionOS 1.0+ · watchOS 9.4+

Controls whether the command is a timed command (using Timed Invoke).

## Declaration

```objectivec
@property (nonatomic, copy, nullable) NSNumber * timedInvokeTimeoutMs;
```

<a id="discussion"></a>

## Discussion

If nil (the default value), a regular invoke is done for commands that do not require a timed invoke and a timed invoke with some default timed request timeout is done for commands that require a timed invoke.

If not nil, a timed invoke is done, with the provided value used as the timed request timeout.  The value should be chosen small enough to provide the desired security properties but large enough that it will allow a round-trip from the server to the client (for the status response and actual invoke request) within the timeout window.

# serverSideProcessingTimeout (Swift)

**Framework:** Matter  
**Kind:** Instance Property  
**Availability:** iOS 18.4+ · iPadOS 18.4+ · Mac Catalyst 18.4+ · macOS 15.4+ · tvOS 18.4+ · visionOS 2.4+ · watchOS 11.4+

Controls how much time, in seconds, we will allow for the server to process the command.

## Declaration

```swift
@NSCopying var serverSideProcessingTimeout: NSNumber? { get set }
```

<a id="discussion"></a>

## Discussion

The command will then time out if that much time, plus an allowance for retransmits due to network failures, passes.

If nil, the framework will try to select an appropriate timeout value itself.

# Document: timedInvokeTimeoutMs

Source path: documentation/matter/mtrovencavityoperationalstateclusterstartparams/timedinvoketimeoutms
Canonical source: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/matter/mtrovencavityoperationalstateclusterstartparams/timedinvoketimeoutms

# timedInvokeTimeoutMs (Swift)

**Framework:** Matter  
**Kind:** Instance Property  
**Availability:** iOS 18.4+ · iPadOS 18.4+ · Mac Catalyst 18.4+ · macOS 15.4+ · tvOS 18.4+ · visionOS 2.4+ · watchOS 11.4+

Controls whether the command is a timed command (using Timed Invoke).

## Declaration

```swift
@NSCopying var timedInvokeTimeoutMs: NSNumber? { get set }
```

<a id="discussion"></a>

## Discussion

If nil (the default value), a regular invoke is done for commands that do not require a timed invoke and a timed invoke with some default timed request timeout is done for commands that require a timed invoke.

If not nil, a timed invoke is done, with the provided value used as the timed request timeout.  The value should be chosen small enough to provide the desired security properties but large enough that it will allow a round-trip from the server to the client (for the status response and actual invoke request) within the timeout window.

# serverSideProcessingTimeout (Swift)

**Framework:** Matter

## Declaration

```swift
@NSCopying var serverSideProcessingTimeout: NSNumber? { get set }
```

<a id="discussion"></a>

## Discussion

The command will then time out if that much time, plus an allowance for retransmits due to network failures, passes.

If nil, the framework will try to select an appropriate timeout value itself.

# Document: timedInvokeTimeoutMs

Source path: documentation/matter/mtrovenmodeclusterchangetomodeparams/timedinvoketimeoutms
Canonical source: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/matter/mtrovenmodeclusterchangetomodeparams/timedinvoketimeoutms

# timedInvokeTimeoutMs (Swift)

**Framework:** Matter  
**Kind:** Instance Property  
**Availability:** iOS 18.4+ · iPadOS 18.4+ · Mac Catalyst 18.4+ · macOS 15.4+ · tvOS 18.4+ · visionOS 2.4+ · watchOS 11.4+

Controls whether the command is a timed command (using Timed Invoke).

## Declaration

```swift
@NSCopying var timedInvokeTimeoutMs: NSNumber? { get set }
```

<a id="discussion"></a>

## Discussion

If nil (the default value), a regular invoke is done for commands that do not require a timed invoke and a timed invoke with some default timed request timeout is done for commands that require a timed invoke.

If not nil, a timed invoke is done, with the provided value used as the timed request timeout.  The value should be chosen small enough to provide the desired security properties but large enough that it will allow a round-trip from the server to the client (for the status response and actual invoke request) within the timeout window.

```

<a id="discussion"></a>

## Discussion

If nil (the default value), a regular invoke is done for commands that do not require a timed invoke and a timed invoke with some default timed request timeout is done for commands that require a timed invoke.

If not nil, a timed invoke is done, with the provided value used as the timed request timeout.  The value should be chosen small enough to provide the desired security properties but large enough that it will allow a round-trip from the server to the client (for the status response and actual invoke request) within the timeout window.
